data.title: Roast My TechStack #2 · April 6, 2026 · Singapore
data.excerpt: Three builders brought three very different stacks: a self-improving order-hub workflow, a Spanish-through-music app, and a drag-node automation tool. This recap preserves the practical decisions, trade-offs, and questions raised in the room.

children.text: A self-improving software workflow: users report issues through a chatbot, complaints become GitHub issues, and an automation loop routes them into Claude Code to generate, apply, and ship fixes — with a human validating before redeploy.
Chatbot intake · GitHub issues · OpenClaw · Claude Code · Human validation

A user complains via the chatbot → the complaint becomes a GitHub issue → an OpenClaw cron pulls the issues → the issue goes into Claude Code → a Claude skill generates and applies a fix → changes push to GitHub → a human tests the software → if solved it redeploys, if not it returns for further fixes.
To improve AI output quality, check out
for better-looking components with less effort.

An app that teaches Spanish through music — pulling real lyrics, front-end design via Stitch, and open-source components to keep the stack light. The roast pushed on where the API calls live and how to keep UI changes verifiable.
LRCLib · Stitch + Google MCP · Heartmula · Open-source streaming · Frontend API calls
is the open-source package to pull lyrics from music. Use
— an open-source music LLM — as an open-source music streaming / YouTube API alternative.
Push the API call to the frontend
to avoid being API-blocked by Google. And add
to check for better UI control — the AI should show its work before you approve it.

An automation tool where you connect workflows by dragging nodes. The roast gave three sharp habits: escalate models deliberately, let AI write your documentation, and make the AI wait for you instead of the other way round.
Drag-and-drop flow · Model escalation · AI documentation
Don't reach for the biggest model for everything
— escalate the model accordingly as the task demands it.
— get the AI to write it for you.
Let the AI wait for you, instead of waiting for the AI.

data.excerpt: Three stacks on the table: a production-style personal LinkedIn analytics pipeline, a caregiver navigation app, and a voice-driven resume. This recap preserves the practical decisions, trade-offs, and questions raised in the room.

$media.alt: Ying Zhao presenting his LinkedIn analytics pipeline at Roast #4

content.alt: Ying Zhao presenting his LinkedIn analytics pipeline at Roast #4

children.text: A production-style personal analytics pipeline for LinkedIn, built with Databricks in a medallion architecture — and optimized for maximum reach. The roast covered getting the data, ETL done right, retries, and the One Big Table trade-off.
Databricks · Medallion ETL · One Big Table · API · Retries & backoff
— when the API doesn't give you what you need.
(gold). Databricks is the cloud-based platform that runs the data analytics and AI workloads.
— especially for LLM calls and APIs. This prevents a huge bill shock when a provider starts failing in burst.
One Big Table Over A Relationship DB
approach beats a relationship database (e.g. Neo4j) for query speed and simplifies data consumption — fewer joins, one place to ask questions of.

$media.alt: Ee One Lim presenting Care Compass at Roast #4

content.alt: Ee One Lim presenting Care Compass at Roast #4

children.text: An app that navigates caregivers to the right support resources — a RAG-over-LLM build that raises reliability over raw generation. The roast dug into RAG vs. web search, dynamic model selection, and where to store the knowledge base.
RAG · n8n · Postgres · Dynamic model selector · Web search
If you have a single source of truth,
RAG is preferred over a raw LLM
— it increases reliability. And if you need the LLM to do a web search,
use a dedicated web search tool
rather than letting the model guess.
to choose the best model per use case. n8n reduces LLM usage overall and can switch between using an LLM web search and RAG depending on the query.
Store The Knowledge Base In Postgres
for the RAG store. For cost efficiency, consider other LLMs for this use case — like GPT-5.4 mini or other open-weight models.
Other tools raised: the eval tool in the Claude platform, and

content.alt: Kaleb presenting the Voice Resume at Roast #4

children.text: A voice-driven resume — an AI-voice interview app that lets employers ask anything and get real-time answers. The roast covered voice recognition, budget compute, text-to-speech, and guardrailing AI applications.

(automatic speech recognition) turns the interview questions into text, and
does the text-to-speech for the answers. The result: employers talk to a resume like it's a candidate.
Oracle Cloud's free tier lasts forever
: 24GB RAM, 4 CPU, and 10TB egress — plenty for a side project with a video-heavy workload.
Always consider guardrails for AI applications, and the simplest way to build them is via a

data.title: Roast My TechStack #6 · June 4, 2026 · Singapore
data.excerpt: Two builds took the heat at SGInnovate: a parallel AI content pipeline and an evaluation harness for AI agents. This recap preserves the practical decisions, trade-offs, and questions raised in the room.

$media.alt: Jesse Sng presenting at Roast #6

content.alt: Jesse Sng presenting at Roast #6

children.text: Brought a content pipeline that fans one piece of source material out into a podcast, blog, images, and audio in parallel. The conversation concentrated on orchestrating parallel generation, engineering error handling so effort is never discarded, and choosing image models when text-in-image matters.
Parallel generation · Fail-continue · Imagen · GPT Image · Remotion · ComfyUI
When you run a parallel workflow — one source, multiple outputs at once — always plan for
up front. The fan-out is the easy part; reassembling coherent pieces from independent branches is where the complexity lives.
Error Management: Continue First, Retry Later
If a branch fails, plan the workflow to
continue first and go back to retry afterwards
. Do not discard the previous effort — partial success is still worth keeping. Fail-continue beats fail-fast when each branch is expensive to produce.
is cheaper for image generation than GPT Image, but it does not support rendering text inside the image. If you need legible text baked into the asset,
remains affordable — or render and superimpose text over the image afterwards to save cost.
For finer control over image aesthetics, explore
for image improvement pipelines. For programmatic video, consider
when the load warrants the heavier machinery.

$media.alt: Gaurav Kumar Manek presenting on evals at Roast #6

content.alt: Gaurav Kumar Manek presenting on evals at Roast #6

children.text: A talk on evaluation for AI agents — where evals overlap with guardrails, how to bound an agent's blast radius, and when a deterministic check beats a model call. The clearest framework of the night for grading agent output.
LLM evals · Guardrails · Deterministic checks · Blast radius
Evals and guardrails can overlap, but they are not the same job. A guardrail can be implemented as deterministic code — it doesn't need to be another model.
Two ways to keep a misbehaving agent from doing damage:
— run agents on isolated resources (a separate Mac mini, a separate cloud account) so a failure can't reach production systems.
— make destructive actions progressive and reversible: draft an email instead of sending it, mark an email instead of deleting it.

data.title: Roast My TechStack #7 · July 2, 2026 · Singapore
data.excerpt: Three builders unpacked an AI-native astrology product, an AI repair loop for Playwright, and a server-first real-time application. This recap preserves the practical decisions, trade-offs, and questions raised in the room.

$media.alt: Kong presenting Zhiji at Roast #7

content.alt: Kong presenting Zhiji at Roast #7

children.text: A solo, non-technical founder building a live, paid AI astrology companion with no human engineer in the loop. Zhiji means "the one who knows you": it calculates a Chinese astrology chart from a birthday, then becomes a companion that knows that chart and the people around it.
Vercel · Vanilla JS · Supabase / Postgres · Stripe · Claude / GPT / DeepSeek

Two constraints shaped everything: Kong is a solo, non-technical founder who has written zero lines of code, and if it breaks, he fixes it with AI. The stack is optimised for exactly one question: can an AI understand, change, and fix it with no human engineer in the loop?

Zhiji evolved through three versions. v0 was screenshots pasted into Claude. v1 added a database for memory. v2 removed the astrology maths from the model, split a fragile single page into separate rooms, and added live streaming. Each version was a wall hit and rebuilt around.
module per room. No React, Vue, bundler, or build step.
routes every reading and chat request, streams over SSE, stamps
, and re-drives failures via recovery sweeps.
~89 deterministic modules do the astrology maths. The model never performs chart calculations. Same input always yields the same chart.
abstracts the model: Sonnet 4.6 default, Opus on chat turns, DeepSeek + GPT in the roster. Auto-fallback on provider outage.
One Supabase / Postgres DB: profiles, frozen readings, idempotent credit ledger, editable doctrine, runtime config, and subscriptions. Row-level security enabled.
Stripe checkout, webhook, and portal. The coin ledger is idempotent per key — a retried webhook cannot double-grant. Paid readings are frozen and cache-keyed, never regenerated.

The astrology engine is homegrown (~89 modules): four pillars, ten gods, hidden stems, 納音, five-element weighting, luck cycles, full 紫微斗數 chart, 神煞, 用神, the 盲派 layer, and 易經 casting. Validated against an external golden reference (bazi.today) and the doctrine master's calibrated set.
Three boundary bugs were found and fixed: the 子時 midnight day-roll, the month solar-term boundary, and 立春-day hour precision.

, used only for raw calendar astronomy (Gregorian ↔ lunar conversion and solar-term instants). If its maths were ever off at a boundary, it would silently tilt every chart. De-risking today: exact-version pin, everything on top is homegrown, and golden-reference validation. Next step: an automated golden-chart regression suite.

Kong coordinates seven specialist AI agents: CPO (product plan), CFO (money), CMO (marketing), UX (user behaviour), CD (design), TM (writes & ships code), and BM (astrology master). They never talk to each other directly. Kong routes work between them using an agent orchestrator and a custom

The principle: explicitly decide when to continue an existing thread, when to clear context, and when to start a new thread. Validate AI-generated architecture by having multiple LLMs critique each other's decisions rather than relying on a single model.
Pre-compute predictable results instead of generating on demand. Use token streaming so users see the response immediately. Evaluate Iris.io as a potential solution.
Use Haiku to periodically compress or summarise conversation memory. Compact before adding back to the context window. Prune unnecessary context to prevent degradation.
Pre-compute frequently requested outputs. Benchmark cheaper models for comparable quality. Per-generation USD is captured in
. Moving astrology off the model made it both cheaper and exact.
Rather than prompting from scratch every time, provide the AI with a mood board, a brand guide, and a design system as persistent references to enforce consistent UI and UX decisions.

Prompt practice: at the end of each week, ask the LLM to review the week's interactions, identify better prompting strategies, and refine techniques based on actual usage rather than theoretical best practices.
is read live, so a flip takes effect instantly. No staged rollout, no review gate, no rollback. This is the first thing Kong would harden.
The base calendar/solar-term library is the one layer Kong didn't write. Version-pinned, but no automated golden-chart net to catch drift.
A 7-agent fleet builds and maintains it; Kong routes between them and has written zero lines. Blind spots he structurally cannot see from inside — hence the roast.

$media.alt: Fernandi presenting Canary Lab at Roast #7

content.alt: Fernandi presenting Canary Lab at Roast #7

children.text: Canary Lab verifies AI output independently before it ships: an AI repair loop for Playwright and a skill for coding tools. The discussion centred on persistent backend services, immutable requirements, inspectable state, Git diffs, and keeping execution deterministic.
Playwright · Agent guardrails · Git diff · Claude CLI
Running long-lived services in the backend instead of the browser allows them to:
Avoid restarting workflows when the frontend reloads.
A common issue is agents modifying requirements while implementing them. Possible guardrails:
Make PRD files read-only for implementation agents.
Separate planning agents from coding agents.
Treat the PRD as the immutable source of truth throughout execution.
bypasses the Claude TUI. It executes prompts directly from the terminal, making it better suited for automation and scripting.
The interactive REPL (TUI) remains useful when you need to interrupt long-running tasks, exercise more control over the execution process, or debug and experiment during development.
Persist data in files rather than purely in memory. Users can directly inspect changes, improving transparency and debuggability.
Fernandi implemented Git diffs so users can compare previous and current data, review exactly what the AI changed, and build trust before accepting modifications.
Inputs are user stories and the existing codebase. The AI predicts deterministic test cases. Users validate results against video recordings or execution evidence.

Only use LLMs where they provide meaningful value. AI generates test cases; test execution remains deterministic. Only failed application logs are sent to the LLM for diagnosis — successful logs are ignored. This minimises token usage while preserving AI assistance where it matters.

$media.alt: Krishna presenting Unfinal and exe.dev at Roast #7

content.alt: Krishna presenting Unfinal and exe.dev at Roast #7

children.text: A server-first approach to real-time products. exe.dev runs services on a VPS, while Phoenix LiveView keeps business logic on the server and handles UI updates. The session also covered research-led UI work, model behaviour, and coding harnesses.
For real-time applications, exe.dev runs services on a VPS, with everything happening on the server rather than in the browser.

Phoenix LiveView allows developers to write only server-side code. Business logic lives entirely on the server. Phoenix automatically handles UI diffing and updates, reducing frontend complexity while enabling real-time interactions.
A heartbeat mechanism keeps WebSocket connections alive, enabling continuous real-time communication between client and server.
Useful design reference libraries to steer AI-generated interfaces toward higher quality:

Instead of asking an LLM to design from scratch: research similar products, gather user feedback and reviews, identify common UI pain points, compile the findings into a comprehensive design prompt, and generate UI based on those insights rather than generic prompts. This grounds the design in real user preferences instead of the model's default patterns.
to interact with websites behind authentication that traditional crawlers cannot access.
observations: they tend to be eager to take action and may begin implementing solutions before fully validating requirements. Additional guardrails or planning steps are needed before execution.
(pi.dev) as a coding harness, compared against
for Codex workflows. Evaluate based on developer experience, reliability, tool integration, and agent orchestration capabilities.
Excludes unknown / self / not-applicable and higher-learning / student orgs.
